instrument.state: Multiple sequential records were formed over overlapping periods under partly shared external influences, but one or more records have uncertain calendar placement or may contain missing or anomalous increments.
instrument.operation: Compare the ordered pattern of increments across independently dated or overlapping records and shift their relative alignment until distinctive multi-year patterns correspond consistently across specimens.
instrument.signal: A particular alignment produces repeated matching temporal patterns across records and exposes otherwise inconsistent missing, extra, or misassigned increments.
instrument.inference: The matching alignment supports assigning specific temporal positions to previously uncertain increments and extending or checking the chronology across overlapping records.
instrument.limit: Local growth disturbances, weak shared environmental signal, short or repetitive patterns, measurement error, incorrect reference chronologies, and insufficient overlap can produce ambiguous or false alignments.

target.question: What relative and absolute chronology can be justified for the undated correspondence bundle?
evidence: Authored synthetic scenario; no claim about a real organization or person.

Several undated letters carry long ordered weekly dispatch-count strips from the same institutional copying office. Dated office ledgers and overlapping strips supply independently authenticated reference series. The strips were attached when each letter was dispatched, as independently documented.

Counts share a historically established scheduling signal. Calibration on separately dated strips and exhaustive competing-offset checks establish distinctive alignment across the supplied overlaps, including identifiable omitted weeks; no unresolved uniqueness or attachment-timing assumption is needed in this synthetic case.

mapping.state: Overlapping measured count sequences associated with letter dispatch have unknown calendar offsets and missing increments.
mapping.operation: Shift the measured sequences against independently dated and overlapping series, compare distinctive multi-week high/low patterns across all witnesses, and identify missing increments; retain supported offsets and reject incompatible alignments.
mapping.signal: Repeated distinctive count-pattern matches consistently support particular offsets and expose missing or misplaced weeks.
mapping.inference: Assign bounded calendar positions to the count increments and, using the independent contemporaneous attachment link, constrain dispatch dates of the correspondence; propagate disagreements into which calendar anchors or letter links to investigate next.
mapping.limit: Weak common signal, repetitive patterns, short overlap, wrong references and missing increments can create false alignment; dispatch dates alone do not establish original composition dates.
